page: Amazon Web Services c9g.8xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the ARM64 architecture, this instance features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs utilizing the Neoverse-V3 ARMv9 model running at 3.3 GHz. The processor configuration includes 64 KB of L1D cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance operates on the Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 17 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in multi-threaded operations and memory efficiency. The server achieves top-tier results in single-threaded gzip compression at 36.46 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 17.26 GB/sec, alongside strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 457.39 GB/sec. Memory performance is highlighted by a top-tier PassMark memory score and cached read-only small block bandwidth of 4319.78 GB/sec, though uncached large block read and write speeds fall into the average range. Database operations and static web serving throughput both rank in the top tier, with static web serving reaching 92.57 GB/sec and Redis SET operations registering a strong 93.19 million operations per second.

Given its compute-focused hardware profile and high-density ARM architecture, the c9g.8xlarge offers high qualitative cost efficiency for multi-threaded workloads that do not require local storage or high RAM-to-vCPU ratios. It is highly suitable for high-throughput static web serving, database operations, and data compression tasks. Additionally, it demonstrates strong performance in physics simulations and medium-sized language model inference, making it a viable option for lightweight AI text generation and parallelized computational workloads.
